blocks.text: Compare one task under all four patterns

Use the same input and reviewed result for each comparison. No AI may mean a person using a checklist, approved template or ordinary tool. An assistant responds to directed work; for your bounded concept, specify whether it only prepares a draft or recommendation. Automation follows defined triggers and rules. An agent may choose several actions within its permissions.

Record fit, limits, permissions and review effort for all four. A simple task may not need AI. Do not assume that an agent label grants any specific capability. Keep expected gains separate from observed results.
Distinguish a routine reminder from an exception

In the fictional case, the company allows a standard reminder only after confirming the invoice, unpaid status, recipient and absence of a dispute or payment arrangement. An ordinary checklist is the baseline. A fixed recurring path may suit ordinary automation; a varied draft may suit an assistant.

An unusual dispute changes the route. Preserve conflicting information and send the case to the accounts coordinator. Do not infer that a missing dispute flag proves no dispute exists. Do not grant sending, payment, balance-changing or refund authority merely because a system could perform those actions.
Make the authority boundary observable

Support prepares information. A recommendation proposes an action with reasons. A decision selects the action. Approval permits it within the approver’s actual authority. Name the role and evidence required at each human checkpoint.

Specify allowed inputs and actions, prohibited actions and access, monitoring owner and review rhythm, stop conditions, and manual fallback. Written instructions must be matched by actual tool access and settings before adoption. Today’s comparison is planning evidence, not authorization to connect or deploy.
Check the feature and update the concept

Record the exact platform claim, official documentation title and URL, actual check date, supported behavior and limits. General documentation does not prove your account’s plan, connector, settings or tested behavior. If no platform is chosen, state that capabilities remain unverified and must be checked before adoption.

For an optional documentation example, Microsoft Learn describes Power Automate triggers, conditions and approval flows. These references establish general features; they do not establish a configured invoice system. Use your chosen platform’s current official documentation. Save the four-way comparison and updated concept in AI Solution Concept and working artifact.
A routine invoice reminder meets a payment dispute

FICTIONAL TRAINING EXAMPLE: A service company permits a standard reminder only when an invoice is seven days overdue, the unpaid balance and recipient are verified, and no dispute or payment arrangement is recorded. The accounts coordinator owns exception review and approval. A customer reports payment, but the record says unpaid. These are fictional company rules, not universal business requirements.

blocks.title: Revised fictional concept
blocks.text: Proposed bounded concept: use a checklist for occasional reminders; consider fixed automation only for repeated verified records. An assistant may prepare a draft from supplied authorized facts. All reminder drafts remain in human review. Conflicting payment information stops the path and returns to the accounts coordinator for manual investigation. No sending, balance change or refund is authorized by this concept.
